clues: This city is the capital of a state in Sudan. Its roads and rail line link the west of the land with the east.
Rain falls here, yet the place still feels like a desert. Strong heat sucks the wet out fast, and a long dry spell runs from fall to spring.
The Egyptians founded the new city here in 1821. Before that, it had grown as a busy stop for trade caravans.
This city was wrecked and left empty in a time of revolt. It was built back up in 1899, when new rulers took charge.
Its markets are famed for gum arabic, grain, oil seeds, and herds. That rich trade marks this crossroads city at once.
